tasks.short: Watch a client's cooking and suggest another method.

steps.what: Observe the client's meal preparation in the kitchen.
inputs: food and pans in this kitchen
outputs: what was seen of this meal preparation

steps.what: Discuss what makes this meal preparation hard for the client.
inputs: what was seen of this meal preparation
outputs: what the client says is hard

steps.what: Suggest alternate methods of food preparation that this kitchen can do.
inputs: what was seen of this meal preparation
what the client says is hard
outputs: alternate method said in the kitchen

tasks.design: The assistant still observes the meal preparation, still discusses it, and still suggests the alternate method in the kitchen. No model drafts the method. No diet, allergy or swallowing note is written, because that would be data concerning health. Nothing in this task is shortened.
tasks.previous_blocker: The alternate method is only clear after the assistant has seen this client's hands, this stove and the food on the counter. A sheet written beforehand has not seen those.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes that look or that talk. A generic method written elsewhere would still have to be judged against this kitchen, which is the task.
tasks.still_hard: A diet limit, a swallowing difficulty or an unsafe pan is easy to miss, and a wrong method can harm the client. That judgement stays in the room.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether this client can manage the method, and saying a simpler one without taking the cooking away from them.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The assistant still spends this time in the kitchen and still chooses the method there.

reach.task: Hear when a cooking difficulty is a safety or nutrition problem
reach.learn: Which observations to pass on, and which methods the assistant may still suggest

reach.task: Show what they can manage at the stove
reach.learn: Not to suggest a method the hands, the diet or this kitchen cannot do

evidence.claim: On a home or group-kitchen visit the assistant watches the meal preparation, talks about what is hard, and suggests another method from what was just seen. Model knowledge.
Data concerning health is a special category of personal data.

assumptions: The boundary is one kitchen visit: observe the meal preparation, discuss it, and suggest alternate methods. No case note is written in this task.

No structured diet, allergy or swallowing record is produced or consumed. If a prescribed diet exists, a dietitian or a social worker wrote it outside this task. This visit does not load it into a system.
No tool is added, so focal upkeep is zero. The legal evidence is why no health note is stored. It is not a reason to cut the visit.
unknowns: Whether this provider forbids the assistant to suggest a method when a dietitian has prescribed the diet.
Whether the visit is in the client's own kitchen or a shared group kitchen.
research_questions: How often an alternate method is blocked because a prescribed diet forbids the assistant to change it?

incremental.description: No meal-method tool is added, so the assistant has no new upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The assistant still observes, still discusses, and still suggests the method in the kitchen. No step is shortened, so no time is saved on a visit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tell tenants where the laundry and playground are.

steps.what: Find the current facts for this building's laundries and playgrounds.
inputs: facility card when the housing officer has written one

steps.what: Inform tenants of those facilities in the building.

tasks.design: The housing officer keeps one facility card: facility name, place, hours, access rule, who to call when it is broken, and the date checked. The assistant reads that card instead of searching old messages, which is the only shorter step. The assistant still informs the tenant in person. A question the card does not answer is asked of the housing officer inside the lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: Laundry hours and playground rules sat in old messages and in memory, so each question started with a search.
tasks.enabler_now: Those facts already belong to the housing officer. Writing them once on a card needs no new system.
tasks.still_hard: A tenant who does not read a card, and a question about today's closure, still needs the assistant to speak. The card is wrong the week the hours change and nobody rewrites it.
tasks.human_edge: Saying the facts so this tenant understands, and noticing when the question is not on the card.
tasks.altitude: The search for standard laundry and playground facts is shorter when the card is current. The assistant still informs every tenant in person and gains no new decision.

reach.task: Keep the facility card current for this building
reach.learn: To check the date on the card, and to ask the officer before informing when the date is old

reach.task: Ask about a laundry or a playground this card does not describe
reach.learn: Not to answer a closure or a broken machine from the card alone

evidence.claim: In supported housing the assistant tells tenants where the laundry and the playground are, usually in the building, after looking in a house folder or an old message. A single current card shortens that look. It does not remove the telling. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one tenant question, or one introduction of a new tenant, about this building's laundries and playgrounds. Informing stays in person and keeps its full time.

Facility card fields are facility name, place, hours, access rule, break-contact and checked date. The producer is the housing officer, when hours or access change. If the card is missing or the question is not on it, the assistant asks the housing officer inside the lookup, before informing.

The inform step does not read the card and uses no system. Reading a current card is why the lookup remains at 60, not at 100: the old-message search drops, and questions the card cannot answer stay in that same step.
The assistant does not rewrite the card. That upkeep is the housing officer's 1.5 hours per 100 assistant hours on this task. The assistant's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this building has a housing officer who will keep the card, or the assistant is the only person who knows the hours.
How often laundry hours or playground access change.
research_questions: Of the questions tenants actually ask, how many are standard facts a card can answer, and how many are today's closure or a broken machine?

incremental.description: The assistant adds no recurring chore. Reading the card is the lookup step.
The housing officer rewrites the facility card when hours, the access rule or the break-contact change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A building with no current card, or a tenant who asks about a closure the card does not list. The assistant still searches and still informs every tenant in person, so almost none of the lookup goes away.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The assistant still watches meal preparation in the kitchen and still informs tenants in person. A facility card, written by the housing officer, shortens only the search for laundry and playground facts. No model drafts a cooking method, and no diet note is stored.
reach: Housing officer: a facility card with a stale checked date. Learn the current break-contact before informing the tenant.
Social worker: a cooking difficulty that is unsafe or a nutrition problem. Learn which observations to pass on rather than only suggesting a method.
Client: a cooking method the hands, the diet or the kitchen cannot do. Learn to drop that method in the room.
skills_to_grow: Reject a facility card whose checked date is old before informing a tenant.
Reject an alternate cooking method the client's hands, diet or kitchen cannot do.
Pass a cooking difficulty that is a safety problem to the social worker instead of treating it as a method tip.
role.ambitious_version: Facility cards at the desk are current. The assistant still speaks to the tenant and still watches the cooking. The meal suggestion and the informing do not move off the person.
